newsitem.title: NORWAY: Storebrand raps investor over shareholding.
newsitem.headline: Storebrand raps investor over shareholding.

text.p: Norwegian insurer Storebrand ASA on Wednesday said it had combined the shareholdings of four major investors into one in what amounted to a crackdown on billionaire entrepreneur Kjell Inge Roekke.
The measure was announced shortly before Storebrand's annual general meeting opened and effectively curbed the voting rights of Roekke and his associates at the meeting.

Storebrand said in a statement its board had decided to count as one group the separate shareholdings of Roekke, his two companies Ivory Enterprises Co and Ivory AS as well as those of Aker RGI, of which Roekke is the main shareholder.
The announcement stripped Aker RGI of about 24 million shares in Storebrand, trimming down the joint shareholdings of the group to 10 percent from 16 percent, a Storebrand spokesman said.
He said Storebrand decided to disqualify Aker RGI's six percent because it was the most recent acquisiton made.
Under Norwegian law, an investor cannot hold more than 10 percent of a financial institution.
Storebrand has been at odds with Roekke and Aker RGI since last week when the insurer dismissed doubts raised by Aker RGI about redeeming Storebrand's preference shares.

Aker RGI top executive Bjoern Rune Gjelsten, a close associate of Roekke, in a newspaper interview had questioned whether the rules for redeeming preference capital in Storebrand complied with securities legislation.
If Aker RGI's opinion prevailed, it could create problems in the proposed merger between Storebrand and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse.
Storebrand said the issuing of short-term preference shares formed a significant part of the refinancing of Storebrand in 1993 following a failed takeover bid in the insurance sector.
